title: Picture Graph Worksheets
intro: Show your student how a graph key connects each symbol to a count.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Read the key together, then count one row. Discuss whether a question asks for one category, all the votes, or the difference between two counts.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Example counts: A = 5, B = 3, C = 4.

The total is 5 + 3 + 4 = 12 votes. The largest group has five votes and the smallest has three, so the difference is 5 − 3 = 2 votes.

Ask your student

What does one block represent?

If your student needs help

If the student counts categories instead of votes, have them touch each block as they count.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each sheet includes two questions about A, two questions about the total, and two questions about the difference between the largest and smallest counts. Every graph has three groups with one through eight votes per group.
